processes.name: Business model
processes.trigger: Use when the requested work concerns business model and needs the following output: Business model canvas and economics table: segment, job, offer, revenue driver, cost driver, partner, advantage, assumption.

steps.instruction: Group buyers by paid problem and purchase context, recording evidence for each segment.
Map each segment to a promised outcome and the delivery mechanism that produces it.
Model revenue as volume times realized price, separating recurring and one-off streams.
List variable costs, fixed costs, delivery partners and capacity dependencies per stream.
Compare advantage against the customer's next-best alternative and identify the assumption most likely to break viability.

processes.output_contract: Business model canvas and economics table: segment, job, offer, revenue driver, cost driver, partner, advantage, assumption.

quality_checks.criterion: Revenue totals reconcile to the stream model.
Every segment has a delivery path and cost owner.
Claimed advantages have evidence or an explicit validation plan.

processes.stop_condition: Do not endorse viability when the delivery mechanism or main cost driver is unknown.

handoff.condition: If the requested scope continues into the next domain; otherwise return the accepted artifact to the orchestrator.

processes.name: Commercial objectives and planning
processes.trigger: Use when the requested work concerns commercial objectives and planning and needs the following output: Commercial plan and scenario workbook: period, target, driver, forecast, capacity gap, priority, owner.

steps.instruction: Translate growth ambitions into revenue, contribution and cash objectives with dates.
Build downside, base and upside forecasts from explicit volume, price and conversion assumptions.
Backsolve required qualified demand and sales workload against available capacity.
Rank product-market combinations by expected contribution and execution feasibility.
Publish a plan with assumption owners, review dates and triggers for replanning.

processes.output_contract: Commercial plan and scenario workbook: period, target, driver, forecast, capacity gap, priority, owner.

quality_checks.criterion: Forecast formulas are reproducible from named inputs.
Sales and fulfillment capacity support the base case or expose a funded gap.
Scenarios vary assumptions rather than applying arbitrary percentage multipliers.

processes.stop_condition: Escalate incompatible revenue targets and delivery capacity to the business owner.

handoff.condition: If the requested scope continues into the next domain; otherwise return the accepted artifact to the orchestrator.

processes.name: Unit economics
processes.trigger: Use when the requested work concerns unit economics and needs the following output: Unit-economics model: cohort, period, customer count, net revenue, variable cost, CAC, cumulative contribution, payback, assumptions.

inputs.description: variable delivery costs and retention history

steps.instruction: Calculate net revenue and contribution per acquired customer, treating refunds and taxes consistently.
Divide allocated acquisition costs by newly acquired customers in the same scope and period.
Estimate cumulative cohort contribution and distinguish observed value from extrapolated lifetime value.
Compare cumulative contribution against acquisition cost to identify payback by offer and channel.
Stress-test retention, gross margin and acquisition cost, then propose viability thresholds.

processes.output_contract: Unit-economics model: cohort, period, customer count, net revenue, variable cost, CAC, cumulative contribution, payback, assumptions.

quality_checks.criterion: No mixing of revenue LTV with contribution-based payback.
Zero or missing denominators return unavailable rather than zero.
Immature cohorts and extrapolation horizons are visible.

processes.stop_condition: Do not recommend scaling from unallocated costs or immature LTV without a bounded pilot.

handoff.condition: If the requested scope continues into the next domain; otherwise return the accepted artifact to the orchestrator.

processes.name: Revenue architecture
processes.trigger: Use when the requested work concerns revenue architecture and needs the following output: Revenue architecture map with stream shares, contribution, expansion paths, dependency exposures and scenario impacts.

steps.instruction: Classify transactions into one-off, recurring and usage revenue with consistent recognition periods.
Calculate portfolio mix and contribution, identifying dependencies between offers.
Map account expansion paths using eligibility and delivered value rather than assumed upsell rates.
Separate partner-sourced revenue from partner fees and overlapping attribution.
Stress-test loss of major customers, partners or products and document diversification options.

processes.output_contract: Revenue architecture map with stream shares, contribution, expansion paths, dependency exposures and scenario impacts.

quality_checks.criterion: Stream shares sum to the scoped total without duplicate transactions.
Recurring revenue excludes one-time fees.
Concentration scenarios quantify exposure and recovery assumptions.

processes.stop_condition: Escalate unreconciled contract and transaction data before presenting concentration as exact.

handoff.condition: If the requested scope continues into the next domain; otherwise return the accepted artifact to the orchestrator.

steps.instruction: Define standard discount bands and calculate margin after each proposed concession.
Specify payment, renewal, cancellation and service terms for qualified review.
Identify markets that can actually be served with current delivery and support.
Match promised service levels to staffing, inventory and lead times.
Define exception thresholds, approvers and expiry dates with a worked example.

processes.output_contract: Commercial policy matrix: offer, market, standard terms, discount ceiling, contribution floor, capacity constraint, exception owner.

quality_checks.criterion: Discount examples respect the approved margin floor.
Every exception has an owner and expiry.
Market eligibility agrees with operational capacity.
